instructions.text:
# Founderealm Lens

This repository carries a map of itself. Read the map before reading source
broadly. Source is the final authority; the map is how you find the right
source fast.

    ./capture    rebuild the map. Run it when the code changed.
    ./search     ask it something. Start with `./search views`.
    ./verify     check the instrument itself, not your code.

## Reading an answer

Every table carries a CAVEAT and it prints with the rows. Read it. Call sites
resolve by NAME, so they are candidates and not proven edges. A null means
never measured, not zero.

ABSENT, BLOCKED and ORPHANED are answers, not errors. They mean nobody
surveyed that ground. Report them as unknown. Do not fill them in.

Use grep when the map says it does not know. That is what the map is for.

## The lenses are examples

`founderealm/lenses/` holds eight small scripts. They are a demonstration of what is
possible, not a fixed set and not a framework.

Write your own. Copy `NEW_LENS.py.example`, declare its `LENS` contract, write
the JSON it promises. `./capture` finds it by reading that declaration. There
is no registry to edit.

Delete the ones you do not want. `./capture` notices: it names the artifacts
nothing produces any more, and it blocks and names any lens whose input is
gone rather than failing on it.

Never hand-edit an artifact. Fix the lens, then capture again.

execution_contract.evidence: how the stage establishes its claims
execution_contract.external_inputs: observed inputs not produced by another stage
execution_contract.invalidates: outputs made stale by a changed input
execution_contract.optional_requires: soft inputs; absence must not block the stage
execution_contract.scope: population the stage is allowed to inspect
execution_contract.trust_tier: provenance tier for the executable lens recipe

call.caveat: RESOLVED BY NAME, not by receiver type. Any object's method of that name lands here, so each row is a CANDIDATE call site and not a proven edge. target=<unresolved> means the grammar put the callee somewhere none of the declared callee fields reached.
call.columns: "file" VARCHAR, "line" INTEGER, "column" INTEGER, "end_line" INTEGER, "end_column" INTEGER, "start_byte" BIGINT, "end_byte" BIGINT, "evidence" VARCHAR, "language" VARCHAR, "target" VARCHAR

dependency.caveat: resolution=resolved means a relative path written in the source was followed from the file that wrote it and landed on a file that exists, so the edge is known. inferred means no path could be followed and a name matched somewhere in the repository, which can be wrong where two files share a name in different packages.

file.caveat: capability=derived_node_type means symbols, imports and calls were read from node type names rather than a curated table. parse_status=ERRORS_PRESENT means the grammar recovered from a syntax error, so records from that file may be incomplete.
file.columns: "file" VARCHAR, "language" VARCHAR, "bytes" BIGINT, "sha256" VARCHAR, "parse_status" VARCHAR, "evidence" VARCHAR, "capability" VARCHAR

impact.caveat: Derived by walking dependency edges backwards from changed files, so it inherits the inferred-edge caveat. depth is hops, not severity. Empty on a first run, when there is no prior run to compare against.
impact.grain: one row per file reached by a change, with its distance

import.caveat: syntax names the node type it came from, or call:<name> when a language spells an import as a function call, as Ruby and Lua do. A grouped import, as Go and Kotlin spell one, yields one row per package rather than one row for the group.
import.columns: "file" VARCHAR, "line" INTEGER, "column" INTEGER, "end_line" INTEGER, "end_column" INTEGER, "start_byte" BIGINT, "end_byte" BIGINT, "evidence" VARCHAR, "language" VARCHAR, "syntax" VARCHAR, "statement" VARCHAR
import.grain: one row per import, include or require

skipped.caveat: Every file that was not parsed, with the reason. These are decisions, not defects: the extension is declared non-source, or no grammar exists for it because it is a data format rather than a language. A reason that does not begin "not parsed:" is something that went wrong and is worth reading. Add an extension to terrain.non_source_extensions to stop seeing it here at all.
skipped.grain: one row per file that was not parsed, with the reason

symbol.caveat: kind is the grammar's own node type with its suffix removed, so it is the grammar's vocabulary and not a normalized one: class, struct, trait and interface all appear as the language spells them. A name of <anonymous> means the grammar declared no name field and no identifier child.
symbol.columns: "file" VARCHAR, "line" INTEGER, "column" INTEGER, "end_line" INTEGER, "end_column" INTEGER, "start_byte" BIGINT, "end_byte" BIGINT, "evidence" VARCHAR, "language" VARCHAR, "kind" VARCHAR, "name" VARCHAR

test.caveat: Discovery is by DIRECTORY AND FILENAME CONVENTION ONLY. Nothing here was executed and no outcome is recorded, so this says a test exists and never that it passes.
test.grain: one row per file that looks like a test

unresolved.caveat: Usually a third-party or standard-library import, which is correct and not a defect. Absence from this table is not evidence an edge was found.
unresolved.grain: one row per import that matched no file in this repository
